entries.originalText: “My Son, in many things it behoveth thee to be ignorant, and to esteem thyself as one dead upon the earth, and as one to whom the whole world is crucified.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, in many things you must remain ignorant and regard yourself as one dead upon the earth, and as one to whom the whole world is crucified.

entries.originalText: Many things also thou must pass by with deaf ear, and must rather think upon those things which belong unto thy peace.
entries.modernizedText: You must also pass many things by with a deaf ear and think instead about the things that belong to your peace.

entries.originalText: It is more profitable to turn away thine eyes from those things that displease, and to leave each man to his own opinion, than to give thyself to discourses of strife.
entries.modernizedText: It is more profitable to turn your eyes away from things that displease you and leave each person to his own opinion than to give yourself to contentious discussions.

entries.originalText: If thou stand well with God and hast His judgment in thy mind, thou wilt verily easily bear to be as one conquered.”
entries.modernizedText: If you stand well with God and keep His judgment in mind, you will very easily bear being treated as one defeated.”

entries.originalText: O Lord, to what have we come?
entries.modernizedText: O Lord, what have we come to?

entries.originalText: Behold a temporal loss is mourned over; for a trifling gain we labour and hurry; and spiritual loss passeth away into forgetfulness, and we rarely recover it.
entries.modernizedText: See how a temporary loss is mourned; for a trifling gain we labor and hurry; yet spiritual loss passes into forgetfulness, and we rarely recover it.

entries.originalText: That which profiteth little or nothing is looked after, and that which is altogether necessary is negligently passed by; because the whole man slideth away to outward things, and unless he quickly recovereth himself in outward things he willingly lieth down.
entries.modernizedText: What profits little or nothing receives attention, and what is altogether necessary is carelessly passed by; because the whole person slips away to outward things, and unless he quickly recovers himself, he willingly lies down among outward things.
